userStories.title: Decisions, executions and expiry record their changes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Emit one transactional approval_request_changed event for each decision, execution and expiry status transition.

**Motivation** — The later features (assistant, fleet, gate) each move a surface onto `ApprovalGate`.

**Approach** — Call sites. Each is inside the transaction, and inside the same `bookkeeping` callback where there is one, right after the write that set the status:

| Service | Where | Status recorded |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ApprovalDecisionService.decide` | after `transition(id, 'pending', …)` | `approved` or `rejected` |
| `ApprovalExecutionService.execute` | after each `transition(id, 'approved', …)`: the pre-check settle, the run's settle, and the failure settle; inside the `txManager.run` closure (which the private `settle` wraps in `bookkeeping`), and only when `transition` returned a record | `failed` or `executed` |
| `ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper.tick` | after each transition | `expired`, or `approved` on timeout |

The decision, execution and sweeper constructors gain a last parameter `events: ApprovalRequestEvents`. US-001 already supplies the gate parameter and module provider. Retain decision-before-execution commit ordering, command rollback/failure settlement, every tick result shape and every existing expectation. Record only a transition's returned record, never an attempted/lost transition.

- `apps/api/src/approvals/approval-decision.service.spec.ts` — new ApprovalDecisionService(...) passes a stub events object with a record spy as the new last argument; existing expectations stay, and the new record cases are added here.
- `apps/api/src/approvals/approval-execution.service.spec.ts` — both new ApprovalExecutionService(...) calls pass a stub events object with a record spy as the new last argument; existing expectations stay, and the new record cases are added here.
- `apps/api/src/approvals/approval-request-expiry.sweeper.spec.ts` — new ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper(...) passes a stub events object with a record spy as the new last argument; every tick result expectation stays, and the new record cases are added here.
- `apps/api/test/integration/approvals/approval-execute.integration.spec.ts` — the bare new ApprovalExecutionService(...) passes app.get(ApprovalRequestEvents, { strict: false }) as the new last argument; its expectations stay.

Add the end-to-end event-order integration case to an existing approval integration spec. Use the P approver fixture: a fresh user bound to the seeded approver role in P AND granted label.delete in P, since approverMustHoldAction defaults to true. Existing service unit tests drive each entry point and assert the events stub receives the actual transitioned status.

**Scope** — In: decision, execution and expiry transaction hooks and updates to existing constructor test seams. Out: event abstraction/open hook (US-001), visibility/routes (US-003–US-005), cancellation (US-006), retry scheduling (US-007) and event consumers (US-011).

**Interface** — `record(request: ApprovalRequestRecord): Promise<void>` on `ApprovalRequestEvents`; each affected constructor appends `events: ApprovalRequestEvents` as its last parameter.

userStories.title: Listing and reading requests over REST
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add authenticated REST list/detail routes with service-enforced visibility, summary/detail DTOs and localized 404 errors.

**Motivation** — The route permission checks (`approval.policy.manage`, the decide route's key): the services check only policy validity, anti-escalation and decide eligibility.

**Approach** — `src/approvals/approval-requests.controller.ts`: `@ApiTags('approvals') @ApiBearerAuth() @Controller('approvals') export class ApprovalRequestsController`, with `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` on each route. Every route of this feature's controllers carries `@ApiOperation` and `@ApiResponse` for each status it answers (`.nax/rules/api-controllers.md`). The principal ref is `{ type: principal.actorType === 'user' ? 'USER' : 'AGENT', id: principal.id }`; a runner principal never reaches these routes, because `CombinedAuthGuard` admits runner keys only on `@RunnerRoute()` routes.

| Route | `@Requires` | Handler | Answer |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /approvals` (`list`) | `'approval.decide', { enforcedBy: 'service' }` | `queries.list(ref, filter, page)` | 200, page of `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto` |
| `GET /approvals/:id` (`get`) | same | `queries.get(ref, id)` | 200, `ApprovalRequestDto` |

DTOs in `src/approvals/dto/`:
- `ListApprovalRequestsQuery extends KodaPageQuery`: `status?` (one of the seven statuses, `@IsIn`), `projectId?` (non-empty string), `permissionKey?` (non-empty string, at most 200), and `mine?: boolean`, documented with `@ApiPropertyOptional({ type: Boolean })` and turned from the query strings `'true'`/`'false'` into a boolean by a `toBoolean` transform like `src/tickets/dto/list-tickets.query.ts` (so the generated CLI type is `boolean`). Any other value is a 400. The controller passes the raw query through `parseQuery`.
- `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.from(record)` has `id`, `permissionKey`, `projectId`, `actorType`, `actorId`, `onBehalfOfType`, `onBehalfOfId`, `origin`, `requiredMode`, `status`, `satisfiedBy`, `approverType`, `approverId`, `expiresAt`, `decidedAt`, `settledAt` and `createdAt` (dates as ISO strings). It has no `input` and no `result`.
- `ApprovalRequestDto.from(detail)` has the summary's fields plus `input`, `result` and `decisions: ApprovalDecisionDto[]` (`id`, `deciderType`, `deciderId`, `decision`, `comment`, `decidedAt`).

`src/approvals/approval-http-errors.ts` exports `rethrowApprovalError(error: unknown): never`. Every handler in this feature's approval and policy controllers catches and passes errors through it:

| Domain error | HTTP |
|:--|:--|
| `ApprovalRequestNotFoundError` | `NotFoundAppException({}, 'approvals.requestNotFound')` (404) |
| anything else | rethrown unchanged |

`src/i18n/en/approvals.json` and `src/i18n/zh/approvals.json` hold the messages, with `-2` and `400` keys for the validation codes, as `permissions.json` does. The English templates are fixed, and the args reach the client only through them (the global filter answers `JsonResponse.Error(code, message)` with no args):
- `requestNotFound.404`: `Approval request not found`

The `zh` file has the same keys and placeholders. The integration ACs compare `message` with the rendered template, as `roles-api.integration.spec.ts`'s `sentence()` helper does. Add only requestNotFound in this story. Use JsonResponse.Ok envelopes and map page records to summary DTOs while retaining the shared page fields. All response DTO properties carry Swagger metadata.

`src/approvals/approval-api.module.ts`: `ApprovalApiModule` imports `ApprovalEngineModule` and `ProjectAccessModule` (the project policy routes' `ProjectMembershipGuard` needs `ProjectAccessService`, as `src/fleet/approvals/approvals.module.ts` imports it) and declares `ApprovalRequestsController` (and the two policy controllers from US-008 and US-010). `AppModule` imports it. Add an Approval requests block to test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts: GET /api/approvals with the admin token answers 200, and without credentials answers 401; existing blocks are unchanged. Add a DB-free approval-api.module.spec.ts compilation case using GlobalStubsModule, not a database integration wiring test. Integration fixtures create fresh users/REST agents and clear all approval decisions, requests and policies per case; open label.delete requests via configurableTestCommand and ApprovalGate.

**Interface** — `rethrowApprovalError(error: unknown): never`; `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.from(record)`; `ApprovalRequestDto.from(detail)`; `ListApprovalRequestsQuery extends KodaPageQuery`; `GET /approvals` and `GET /approvals/:id` use the query service from US-003.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the authenticated decision route, delegating visibility and decision eligibility to the existing services.

**Motivation** — The route permission checks (`approval.policy.manage`, the decide route's key): the services check only policy validity, anti-escalation and decide eligibility.

**Approach** — Extend `src/approvals/approval-requests.controller.ts` with the decide route:

| `POST /approvals/:id/decisions` (`decide`), `@HttpCode(200)` | `'approval.decide', { enforcedBy: 'service' }` | `queries.get(ref, id)`, then `decisions.decide(id, dto.decision, dto.comment ?? null)` | 200, `ApprovalRequestDto` of the returned request with its decisions |

- `DecideApprovalRequestDto`: `decision` (`'approve' | 'reject'`, `@IsIn`) and `comment?` (string, at most 2000 characters).

`src/approvals/approval-http-errors.ts` exports `rethrowApprovalError(error: unknown): never`. Every handler in this feature's approval and policy controllers catches and passes errors through it:

| Domain error | HTTP |
|:--|:--|
| `ApprovalRequestNotFoundError` | `NotFoundAppException({}, 'approvals.requestNotFound')` (404) |
| `ApprovalRequestNotPendingError(status)` | `ConflictAppException({ status }, 'approvals.notPending')` (409) |
| `ApprovalRequestExpiredError` | `ConflictAppException({}, 'approvals.expired')` (409) |
| `ApprovalDecideForbiddenError(reason)` | `ForbiddenAppException({ reason }, 'approvals.decideForbidden')` (403) |
| anything else | rethrown unchanged |

The English templates are fixed, and the args reach the client only through them (the global filter answers `JsonResponse.Error(code, message)` with no args):
- `notPending.409`: `The approval request is already {status}`
- `expired.409`: `The approval request has expired`
- `decideForbidden.403`: `You cannot decide this approval request: {reason}`

The `zh` file has the same keys and placeholders. The integration ACs compare `message` with the rendered template, as `roles-api.integration.spec.ts`'s `sentence()` helper does. Keep the requestNotFound mapping from US-004. Use the app's existing ConflictAppException if no platform equivalent exists. Each route has @UseGuards(RequiresGuard), @ApiOperation and @ApiResponse for every answered status; return the JsonResponse.Ok detail, including the returned request and its current decisions. The principal ref is `{ type: principal.actorType === 'user' ? 'USER' : 'AGENT', id: principal.id }`.

US-005 only: the decide route checks visibility, then calls `decide`, in two steps; a request that becomes invisible between them (a binding removed) is still decided under `decide`'s own eligibility check, which re-reads the decider's keys.

Use real HTTP integration tests with fresh principals/REST agents, per-case decision/request/policy deletion and a registered/reset configurable label.delete command. The P approver has seeded approver plus label.delete in P. The global non-admin decider sees the project request but lacks the project action key: return the engine's missing-action-permission 403, not a visibility 404.

userStories.title: Cancelling one's own request
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let a requester withdraw its pending approval under a new implicit permission with atomic event and audit recording.

**Motivation** — Cancelling a request (the actor withdrawing it).

**Approach** — **Catalog.** `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` gains `'approval.request.cancel': 'any'`, and `IMPLICIT_KEYS` gains `'approval.request.cancel'`. It is not role-grantable and not approvable (access `implicit`).

**Error.** `src/approvals/domain/approval.errors.ts` gains `export class ApprovalCancelForbiddenError extends Error { constructor(readonly id: string) }`, in the same shape as its siblings.

**Service.** `ApprovalDecisionService.cancel(requestId: string, now?: Date): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord>`. The caller is the current context's actor. In one `txManager.run`:
1. `lockById(requestId)`. When it is missing, throw `ApprovalRequestNotFoundError`.
2. A status other than `pending` throws `ApprovalRequestNotPendingError(status)`.
3. The caller must be a `USER` or `AGENT` equal to the request's actor, or equal to its `onBehalfOf` when the actor is `SYSTEM/assistant`. Otherwise throw `ApprovalCancelForbiddenError(requestId)`. A `SYSTEM` or `RUNNER` caller is always refused.
4. `transition(id, 'pending', { status: 'cancelled', settledAt: now })`.
5. `events.record(cancelled)`.
6. `AuditRecorder.record({ key: 'approval.request.cancel', resourceType: 'approval-request', resourceId: id, projectId, summary: 'cancelled <permissionKey>' })`.

Nothing is written when a step refuses.

| Route | `@Requires` | Handler | Answer |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /approvals/:id/cancel` (`cancel`), `@HttpCode(200)` (US-006) | `'approval.request.cancel'` | `queries.get(ref, id)`, then `decisions.cancel(id)` | 200, `ApprovalRequestDto` |

Every route uses @UseGuards(RequiresGuard), @ApiOperation and @ApiResponse for each status. The principal ref is `{ type: principal.actorType === 'user' ? 'USER' : 'AGENT', id: principal.id }`. Load the detail through the query service before mutation so missing/invisible requests are 404, then return JsonResponse.Ok with the cancelled request and its decisions. Extend rethrowApprovalError with `ApprovalCancelForbiddenError` → `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'approvals.cancelForbidden')` (403); retain requestNotFound and notPending mappings, and rethrow unknown errors unchanged.

- `cancelForbidden.403`: `Only the requester can cancel this approval request`

Add this exact English template to en/approvals.json and matching zh keys/placeholders. A pending request past expiresAt may still be cancelled.

Update catalog.spec.ts's NEW_KEY_SCOPES copy and IMPLICIT_KEY_LIST, so its catalog-equals-derivation and length assertions hold with one more key. Regenerate permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json with the role-matrix spec's update mode: every role gains only the approval.request.cancel implicit column in both cells, as session.logout has; no other cell changes. Extend approval-decision.service.spec.ts without changing its existing decide expectations. Integration cases use REST agents created by POST /api/agents, fresh principals, per-case approval cleanup and the registered/reset label.delete command.

**Scope** — In: implicit catalog key/snapshot, cancel error/service/route, transactional event/audit, localization and cancellation behavior. Out: decide changes (US-005), stale retry (US-007), admin cancellation of another's request and testing the cancellation race itself.

**Interface** — `ApprovalDecisionService.cancel(requestId: string, now?: Date): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord>`; `export class ApprovalCancelForbiddenError extends Error { constructor(readonly id: string) }`; `POST /approvals/:id/cancel`.

userStories.title: Retrying a stale approval
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recover approved requests left unexecuted after a process stop using the existing expiry sweeper interval.

**Motivation** — A retry path for a request left `approved` when the process stopped between the decide commit and `execute`.

**Approach** — `PrismaApprovalRequestRepository.findStaleApproved(before: Date, limit: number)` answers requests with status `approved` and `decidedAt <= before`, oldest `decidedAt` first, at most `limit`.

`ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper` gains:
```ts
export const STALE_APPROVED_AFTER_MS = 300_000;
retryStale(now = new Date()): Promise<{ retried: number; failed: number }>;
```
`retryStale` opens its own `runAsSystemWriter(this, …)` scope, as `tick` does, and inside it reads `findStaleApproved(new Date(now.getTime() - STALE_APPROVED_AFTER_MS), MAX_PER_TICK)` and calls `execution.execute(id, now)` for each request, one after another:
- `execute` returns (any terminal status): `retried + 1`.
- `execute` throws `ApprovalRequestNotPendingError` (someone else settled it): no count, and the loop continues.
- Any other throw: `failed + 1`, a `warn` log with the request id, and the loop continues.

The interval that `onModuleInit` starts runs `tick()`, then `retryStale()`, each with its errors caught and logged as today.

The retry runs in the expiry sweeper. It uses the same interval and the same `@SystemWriter('system.approval.expire')` class: that writer already settles requests. `retryStale` is a second method, so `tick`'s result shape is unchanged. 5 minutes (`STALE_APPROVED_AFTER_MS = 300_000`) is long past any in-flight execution.

Keep tick and existing repository methods unchanged apart from the US-002 event hooks already present. Add retry unit/fake-timer cases to approval-request-expiry.sweeper.spec.ts, including a findStaleApproved stub, while preserving every tick expectation. DB integration cases use a registered/reset label.delete test command and requests opened by a fresh permitted agent before setting approved/decidedAt through fixtureDb. Clear decisions, requests and policies before each case. No schema/index migration is added.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register an MCP-only approval inbox tool for every authenticated agent and append it after the assistant registrations.

**Motivation** — Each needs these routes, the inbox reads and the notifications to exist first, so that a request they open can be seen and decided.

**Approach** — `src/approvals/mcp/approval-mcp-tools.ts`: `@Injectable() export class ApprovalMcpTools`, with constructor `(queries: ApprovalRequestQueries, decisions: ApprovalDecisionService)`. `ApprovalEngineModule` provides and exports it.

```ts
registrations(principal: AgentPrincipal): McpToolRegistration[];
```

At this story's stage registrations returns only koda_list_approvals, matching AC-1; US-013 extends it to [koda_list_approvals, koda_decide_approval] in that order. Do not add a decide stub or expose a thread assistant tool in this story.

Each handler runs inside `runWithActionContext({ actor: { type: 'AGENT', id: principal.id }, origin: 'mcp' }, …)`, and answers `toMcpToolResult({ content, isError })`. The principal ref is `{ type: 'AGENT', id: principal.id }`.

- **`koda_list_approvals`**:
  - Input schema `{ status?: one of the seven statuses, mine?: boolean, page?: integer >= 1 }`, `additionalProperties: false`.
  - It calls `queries.list(ref, { status, mine }, { current: page ?? 1, size: 20 })`.
  - The content has one line per request: `<id> <status> <permissionKey> project=<projectId or global> actor=<actorType>/<actorId> requires=<requiredMode> expires=<expiresAt ISO>`.
  - When more pages exist, the content ends with `next page: <n>`. An empty page answers `no approval requests`.
  - The tool checks its own input (the server passes every argument through): `status` outside the seven statuses answers `invalid_input: status`, `page` that is not an integer >= 1 answers `invalid_input: page`, and `mine` that is not a boolean answers `invalid_input: mine`, each with `isError: true` and no `queries.list` call. userStories.title: The MCP decide tool
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the second MCP-only approval tool for deciding visible requests with explicit validation and stable tool-level errors.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p3-approval-core` (PR #338, `38d435cb`) built the policy model, the resolver, the gate, deciding, executing and expiry, but it exposes services only.

**Approach** — Extend `src/approvals/mcp/approval-mcp-tools.ts`, provided and exported by ApprovalEngineModule, so:

```ts
registrations(principal: AgentPrincipal): McpToolRegistration[];   // [koda_list_approvals, koda_decide_approval], in this order
```

Each handler runs inside `runWithActionContext({ actor: { type: 'AGENT', id: principal.id }, origin: 'mcp' }, …)`, and answers `toMcpToolResult({ content, isError })`. The principal ref is `{ type: 'AGENT', id: principal.id }`.

- **`koda_decide_approval`**:
  - Input schema `{ id: string 1..64, decision: 'approve' | 'reject', comment?: string <= 2000 }`, required `id` and `decision`.
  - It calls `queries.get(ref, id)`, then `decisions.decide(id, decision, comment ?? null)`, and answers `<id> <status>` with `isError: false`.
  - The tool answers these errors with `isError: true`:
    - `invalid_input: id`, `invalid_input: decision` or `invalid_input: comment`, for input that breaks the schema. The tool checks the input itself, because the server passes every argument through (`DELEGATE_VALIDATION_TO_EXECUTOR`).
    - `not_found` for `ApprovalRequestNotFoundError`.
    - `not_pending: <status>` and `expired`.
    - `forbidden: <reason>` for `ApprovalDecideForbiddenError`.
    - Any other error is logged at `error` and answered as `error: koda_decide_approval failed`.

The tool descriptions:
- `koda_decide_approval`: "Approve or reject one pending approval request by its id. An approval runs the requested action at once; the answer is the request's new status. This agent may decide a request only when its permissions and the request's policy allow it; it may confirm its own request only when the request requires `self`."

Keep the US-012 list handler and controller wiring, but update intermediate list-only test expectations to the final two-tool ordering when they assert full registrations or the last tool. The US-012 list tool still remains after every assistant tool; koda_decide_approval is now after it. test/integration/fleet/mcp-route.integration.spec.ts AC-5's tools/list expectation also ends with koda_decide_approval. test/integration/fleet/permissions-mcp-tools.integration.spec.ts AC-3's and AC-6's expected lists also end with koda_decide_approval. Both registrations are offered to every agent independently of assistant tool permission visibility; queries.get and decisions.decide enforce visibility and eligibility. Do not route these calls through AssistantToolExecutor or expose them to the thread assistant.

Integration tests enable MCP_ENABLED and use a REST agent granted label.delete and approval.decide in P to decide a request opened by another agent through the registered/reset test command. Verify the stored request through fixtureDb after tools/call. Use fresh principals and clear all approval decisions, requests and policies per case. Missing/invisible and malformed-input failures must never call decide or mutate the request.

**Scope** — In: decide registration/validation/action context, visibility-before-decision, stable errors and final MCP tool ordering. Out: reimplementing engine authorization, changing the list format (US-012), per-tool permission visibility, assistant thread approval tools and moving PendingAction/FleetApproval.
